audit_scope: 7 P0 Operational Blockers for Production Readiness

evidence_from_repo: DATABASE_URL required at build time: YES (build fails without it)
required_external_services: PostgreSQL 14+ (or Neon, Supabase, RDS, managed provider)
Network connectivity from production network to database
required_commands: npx prisma migrate deploy (run once in production)
npm run db:migrate:deploy (alternative via npm script)
required_verification: DATABASE_URL resolves and is reachable from production network
All 37 migrations apply successfully
Database schema matches prisma/schema.prisma
Foreign keys and indexes created
Connection pooling configured (for Neon, use pooler connection string)
p0_blockers.risk_if_unfixed: Application will not start. All database operations fail. Customers cannot access system.
p0_blockers.exact_fix_or_operator_action: 1) Provision PostgreSQL database (self-managed, Neon, Supabase, RDS, etc.). 2) Generate connection string with sslmode=require if using managed service. 3) Set DATABASE_URL env var in production secrets manager. 4) Run 'npx prisma migrate deploy' once during deployment. 5) Verify with health check endpoint.

evidence_from_repo: Migration scripts in package.json: YES (db:migrate:deploy, db:migrate:dev)
Migration deployment in CI docs: referenced in DEPLOYMENT_RUNBOOK.md
Rollback procedure for migrations: NOT DOCUMENTED
required_commands: npx prisma migrate status (verify all migrations applied)
required_verification: All 37 migrations listed in prisma/migrations/ apply without error
Each migration completes in <10 seconds
No migration conflicts (multiple branches changing schema)
Post-deployment: verify schema with 'npx prisma validate'
Smoke test: health check endpoint returns 200
p0_blockers.risk_if_unfixed: Migrations fail during deployment, application starts with stale schema, database constraints missing, data corruption possible
p0_blockers.exact_fix_or_operator_action: 1) Add DATABASE_URL to production env. 2) Run 'npx prisma migrate deploy' during deployment pipeline (AFTER docker push, BEFORE app start). 3) Capture output and verify no errors. 4) If migration fails, rollback database from backup and re-deploy previous version. 5) Document the specific git commit hash migrations were deployed from.

required_external_services: Secrets manager (AWS Secrets Manager, GitHub Secrets, Vault, HashiCorp Consul, etc.)
required_commands: npm run validate:deployment (checks required env vars at startup)
required_verification: All required env vars present in production
No .env files in production (use secrets manager)
AUTH_SECRET is 32+ random characters
DATABASE_URL has sslmode=require (for cloud databases)
STRIPE keys match live account (not test keys)
Application starts without 'missing env var' errors
Audit logging enabled in production
p0_blockers.risk_if_unfixed: Application fails to start. Stripe integration fails. Auth is broken. Sensitive data exposed in logs.
p0_blockers.exact_fix_or_operator_action: 1) Create .env.production with all required vars (or use secrets manager). 2) For Stripe: log in to Stripe dashboard, copy live API keys. 3) Generate random AUTH_SECRET: 'openssl rand -base64 32'. 4) For SENTRY_DSN: create Sentry project, copy DSN. 5) Verify at deployment time: npm run validate:deployment
p0_blockers.repo_side_fix: .env.example updated with all required production variables

p0_blockers.area: Stripe Billing and Webhook Runtime Readiness
evidence_from_repo: Stripe SDK installed: YES (@stripe/stripe-js, stripe package)
required_external_services: Stripe account with live API keys
Stripe webhook registered to production domain
Public HTTPS endpoint for webhook receiver
required_commands: npm run test:stripe-sim (verify webhook logic locally)
required_verification: Stripe SDK is initialized with live keys (not test keys)
POST /api/webhooks/stripe accepts Stripe webhooks
Webhook signature verification passes for live Stripe webhooks
Webhook events (customer.subscription.created, etc.) are processed
Idempotency: duplicate webhook delivery processed only once
Max retry: webhook dead-lettered after 5 failed attempts
Stripe dashboard shows webhook endpoint registered and recent deliveries successful
p0_blockers.risk_if_unfixed: Payment webhooks not received → subscriptions not activated. Duplicate webhooks → charges duplicated. Webhook failures not retried → customers not onboarded.
p0_blockers.exact_fix_or_operator_action: 1) Log in to Stripe dashboard (live account). 2) Navigate to Developers > Webhooks. 3) Add endpoint: https://yourdomain.com/api/webhooks/stripe. 4) Select events: customer.subscription.*, payment_intent.*. 5) Copy webhook signing secret. 6) Set STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET env var. 7) Test webhook delivery from Stripe dashboard. 8) Verify webhook is received and processed by checking app logs.
p0_blockers.repo_side_fix: docs/STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SETUP.md created with step-by-step Stripe dashboard configuration

evidence_from_repo: Error tracking stub: src/infra/error-tracking.ts (Sentry commented out)
APM agent integrated: NO (requires agent setup)
required_external_services: Error tracking service (Sentry, Rollbar, or cloud provider's built-in)
APM/metrics service (Datadog, New Relic, CloudWatch, Prometheus)
Log aggregation (CloudWatch Logs, ELK, Datadog, Grafana Loki)
Alerting service (PagerDuty, Opsgenie, CloudWatch Alarms, etc.)
required_commands: npm run validate:deployment (verify monitoring env vars)
required_verification: Errors are sent to error tracking system (Sentry)
Metrics are exported to metrics service (Datadog, CloudWatch)
Logs appear in log aggregation system with proper timestamps and levels
Health check endpoint returns database latency, memory usage, uptime
Critical error alerts firing for error rate >5%, database downtime
Response time alerts firing for p95 latency >2s
Disk space alerts firing for <20% free space
p0_blockers.risk_if_unfixed: Production errors go unnoticed. No visibility into performance. Cannot debug production issues. SLA violations undetected.
p0_blockers.exact_fix_or_operator_action: 1) Choose monitoring stack (e.g., Datadog, New Relic, CloudWatch). 2) Create project/account in chosen service. 3) For Sentry: npm install @sentry/nextjs, create Sentry project, copy DSN. 4) For Datadog: npm install @datadog/browser-rum, create API key. 5) Set env vars in production. 6) Deploy and verify errors/metrics reach monitoring service. 7) Create alert rules in monitoring service (error rate, latency, disk space). 8) Configure on-call rotation in PagerDuty or Opsgenie.
p0_blockers.repo_side_fix: docs/MONITORING_SETUP.md created with integration instructions for major providers

p0_blockers.risk_if_unfixed: Failed deployment cannot be reversed. Data corruption persists. Customer trust damaged. RTO/RPO SLAs violated.
p0_blockers.exact_fix_or_operator_action: 1) Before deployment: run backup script and verify backup file >1MB. 2) Document current git commit SHA deployed to production. 3) If deployment fails: stop application, restore database from backup, git revert to previous commit, redeploy. 4) Test rollback procedure in staging. 5) Create runbook: docs/ROLLBACK_RUNBOOK.md with specific commands for your infrastructure.
p0_blockers.repo_side_fix: docs/ROLLBACK_RUNBOOK.md created with detailed procedures; backup scripts validated
